correctness.rationale: The residual identity \(r^+=A^{1/2}(I-C)A^{-1/2}r\) is exact. Submultiplicativity gives the universal factor \(\delta\sqrt{\kappa_2(A)}\). The \(2\times2\) construction with a coordinate-swapping symmetric contraction attains equality, so the constant and the nonexpansion frontier are sharp. In the \(A^{-1}\)-residual norm the same step contracts by at most \(\delta\), proving that the Euclidean spike is a metric/similarity effect rather than a failure of spectral convergence.

value.rationale: Spectral equivalence and preconditioned condition numbers are standard design diagnostics, while the ordinary residual norm is a standard stopping diagnostic. The theorem shows exactly when those two diagnostics are compatible for one Richardson correction and when they are not: a preconditioner can be spectrally excellent and energy-contracting yet still increase the measured Euclidean residual. The sharp two-condition-number frontier and minimal \(2\times2\) equality case give a concrete criterion rather than a generic nonnormality warning.
